questions.question_text: A curve satisfies $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2y+10}$ and passes through $(4,-2)$. Find $y$ as a function of $x$.

options.why: Chose the negative branch, which gives $y=-8$ at $x=4$ instead of the required $-2$.
Made a sign slip completing the square, writing $\sqrt{x+C-25}$ instead of $\sqrt{x-C+25}$.
Made both slips: the sign inside the surd and the wrong branch of the square root.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dx}{dy}=2y+10$
$x=\displaystyle\int(2y+10)\,dy$
$=y^2+10y+C$
$4=4-20+C$
$C=20$
$x=y^2+10y+20$
$y^2+10y+(20-x)=0$
$y=\dfrac{-10\pm\sqrt{100-4(20-x)}}{2}$
$y=-5\pm\sqrt{5+x}$
At $x=4$ the branches give $-5+3=-2$ and $-5-3=-8$, so the positive branch passes through $(4,-2)$.
$y=-5+\sqrt{x+5}$
